new_entities.name: Modafinil for narcolepsy type 1
new_entities.description: Use of modafinil to improve daytime wakefulness in narcolepsy type 1 or older pre-orexin narcolepsy cohorts largely corresponding to narcolepsy with cataplexy.

new_entities.name: Wakefulness
new_entities.description: Objective or subjective maintenance of daytime alertness, often measured with the Maintenance of Wakefulness Test or related sleepiness scales.

edges.effect_quant: A 2010 meta-analysis of 9 trials involving 1,054 patients found modafinil improved ESS by 2.73 points and MWT by 2.82 minutes versus placebo. In long-term randomized withdrawal, continued modafinil maintained MWT at 16.4 minutes versus 9.7 with placebo and lowered ESS from 15.4 to 13.2.
edges.population: adults with narcolepsy, especially classic narcolepsy with cataplexy corresponding most closely to modern narcolepsy type 1
edges.mechanism: Modafinil promotes wakefulness through dopaminergic and other arousal-network effects without directly treating the REM-intrusion biology that drives cataplexy.
edges.summary: This is a solid protective wakefulness edge. Modafinil consistently improves objective and subjective daytime alertness in narcolepsy, but it is primarily a sleepiness treatment rather than a full-spectrum narcolepsy therapy.
edges.caveats: Much of the foundational trial literature predates the modern type 1/type 2 classification, so the evidence is not perfectly phenotype-pure. Benefit is strongest for excessive daytime sleepiness and much weaker for cataplexy itself.

evidence.citation: GolickiD et al 2010 Med Sci Monit
